text.title: plan.md Structure Decision Tree
text.summary: Lifecycle gate first (a feature in todo/ or in-progress/, not docs-only, not a CR / BUG), then the trivial test on task count and new contracts. Every conclusion references a rule id from 01-core-rules.xml.

decision-tree.root-question: Is the work a feature in `features/todo/` or `features/in-progress/` that changes code (not documentation-only, not a CR / BUG)?

branch.conclusion: Documentation-only feature — no plan needed. CR / BUG — wrong lifecycle, use cr-bug-tracking.

branch.question: Does the feature have ≤3 tasks AND introduce no new contract / schema / sequencing constraint — and can you say so in one sentence?

branch.when: task_count <= 3 AND new_contract == false AND one_sentence_answer == true
branch.conclusion: Skip plan.md. The spec.md task checklist is the plan; record the one-sentence reason.
Write plan.md with `## Design` and `## Execution Plan` (steps 2-5 of 04-procedure). Feature-scoped contracts only; system-wide ones stay in project-spec/.
You cannot say "trivial" in one sentence, so it is not — write plan.md.
Merge the two files into plan.md now; the two-file shape is forbidden going forward and drifts within a feature.

text.example: inputs: {feature=true, task_count=6, new_contract=true (signature verification, idempotency)} q-feature -> true q-trivial -> task_count >= 4 OR new_contract == true => conclusion r-two-h2-mandatory: write plan.md — Design (contract, schema, sequencing) + Execution Plan (waves, T01-T06, risks, rollback).
